title: Magic Backpacks
description: Learn how to store multiple items in order inside a single variable using Lists!

content.value: So far, our variables (magic boxes) could only hold one thing at a time. What if we want to store all of our favorite toys? We can use a Magic Backpack (called a List)! Lists can store lots of items in a specific order.
We create a list by wrapping our items in square brackets `[ ]` and separating them with commas.

To grab an item from the backpack, we use its Index (its slot number). BUT BE CAREFUL! Computers are quirky and they start counting slots from 0! Slot 0 is the first item, Slot 1 is the second item, and so on.

toys = ["Lego", "Teddy Bear", "Action Figure"]
print(toys[0])  # Prints Lego
print(toys[2])  # Prints Action Figure
If you get a new toy, you can put it in your backpack using the `.append()` command!

toys = ["Lego", "Teddy Bear"]
toys.append("Water Gun")
print(toys)  # Prints: ['Lego', 'Teddy Bear', 'Water Gun']

quiz.question: What index does the first item in a Python list start at?
quiz.explain: Python counts from 0, so the first item is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on.

quiz.question: Which method is used to add an item to the end of a list?
quiz.explain: `append()` adds an item to the end of a list. `insert()` adds at a chosen spot, and `add()` isn't a list method.
